A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FK steering research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-image, text-quality, toxicity-control, ImageNet, and diversity experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical evaluations, revises the text results, and adds a text-to-image gradient-guidance comparison in Table 3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the reward-tilted target, potential choices, intermediate rewards, and proposal options remain unchanged. The new gradient-guidance experiment evaluates an option already described in v1, including Appendix C.1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same image-prompt benchmarks, prompted text-quality and toxicity tasks, OpenWebText reward-training data, and ImageNet conditional generation. The added guidance comparison uses existing text-to-image coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 3 newly compares ImageReward gradient guidance against FK steering on SDv1.5. Although v1 evaluated gradient guidance for text toxicity, it did not include this comparator in the corresponding text-to-image evaluation. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The added SDv1.5 comparison evaluates single-sample gradient guidance and four-particle FK with guided versus unguided proposals, reporting quality and latency. This adds a controlled experimental configuration; the previously documented prompts, metrics, sampling schedules, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 Table 3 adds an analysis of whether gradient-guided proposals improve FK steering and at what sampling-time cost. Existing potential-choice, intermediate-reward, particle-diversity, and resampling analyses remain, including those in Appendices A and D.

E5.justification: v4 Tables 4 and 6 explicitly report averages over three seeds; corresponding v1 Tables 3 and 5 do not specify repeated-run counts. This establishes newly reported seed averaging, not an explicit increase from a known previous count. No dispersion estimates or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Both main text-result tables are substantially revised, and v4 Table 3 adds guidance-quality and timing results. For SSD-LM with CoLA rewards, FK(k=4) versus BoN(n=8) changes from 97.7 versus 96.0 to 95.7 versus 97.2, reversing the ranking. MDLM with eight particles and many-sample rewards changes from 69.7% to 64.7% guidance-classifier toxicity. These are revised reported estimates, now identified as three-seed averages, rather than demonstrated method improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the locally tilted-conditional presentation with explicit intermediate FK path distributions and their recursive construction. v4 equations 6-7 also derive the particle weights through a path-density ratio. The target constraint, potential definitions, and cited convergence guarantee remain; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The introduction revises the headline toxicity result from 69.7% to 64.7%, and the conclusion adds a claim that FK steering can improve preference-learning sample generators. The central claims about general steering, inference-time scaling, and smaller models outperforming larger models remain.

C2.justification: v4 adds the interpretation that gradient-guided proposals can further improve quality while increasing computation and latency. It also replaces toxicity 'accuracy' language with the fraction of generations labeled toxic. Existing limitations concerning reward quality, diversity, and computational tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: Appendices A-C retain the hardware and parallelization information, decoding and resampling hyperparameters, toxicity-reward training procedure, and checkpoint links. The code link is unchanged. The new guidance comparison supplies results without additional implementation instructions or guidance-specific hyperparameters.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work more explicitly position FK steering as generalizing previous FK-based conditional sampling. Added references include Chung et al., Janati et al., Zheng Zhao et al., and additional SMC and preference-learning sources; the Liu and Liu reference is removed. The existing TDS/SVDD positioning largely remains.

P1.justification: The introduction, related-work discussion, and Section 3.3 receive localized rewrites, with small conclusion additions and terminology corrections. The affiliation numbering is corrected. Overall section organization and most main-text and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 3, shortens and groups method labels in the text-result tables, and revises their captions. Existing figures and tables shift with pagination, but the figures, including appendix sampling examples, retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: The added guidance-versus-cost comparison, explicit three-seed reporting, and clearer FK derivation and research positioning modestly strengthen the paper. Benefits are limited by absent uncertainty estimates and incomplete synchronization of prose with revised results: Section 4.1 still quotes old MDLM scores and broadly claims superiority over twice-budget best-of-n, despite reversed rankings in Table 4. These reporting defects temper the gains without outweighing the useful additions.
